value.rules_markdown:
- Use `snake_case` for modules and files, `PascalCase` for types.
- Return `Result<T>` using the crate error type from `src/error.rs`.
- Every file opens with a `//!` module doc describing its role and feature gating.
- Comments explain the decision, not the code; say why a flag or ordering is load-bearing.
- Public items carry doc comments; Clap fields use `///` for help text.
- Tests live in-crate as `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`, moving to a sibling file when they grow; no `tests/` directory.
- Every port has an always-compiled offline mock; `MockForge` records what would have been written.
- Lane behaviour is covered by golden tests: fixture diff plus canned model response.
- Maintain at least 80% coverage for meaningful library behaviour.
- Keep every Markdown file at 500 lines or fewer; split into focused files when a topic grows past that.
- The model never holds a write token; lanes run against a read-only checkout.
- Contributor code is never executed; we read the diff and tree, not build or run scripts.
- Pull request bodies, comments and diffs are untrusted input; fence and label them as data in prompts.
- Secrets found by scanners are reported by type and location only; values never reach comments, summaries, or logs.
- Use concise, imperative commit subjects; commit each coherent slice on its own.
- Pull requests state what changed, any behaviour change, and how it was verified.
- `src/` is the single crate; one responsibility per module, core types in `types.rs`, each port as one trait in one file.
- Every subcommand is declared even before its milestone lands, for stable script surfaces.
- A preset is a folder with `preset.toml`, `README.md`, and optional prompt overrides; adding a preset is a new folder, never a new module.
- `vendor/tinyagents` is a git submodule; never edit here, change upstream and bump the pin.
- Examples are declared explicitly in `Cargo.toml` with `required-features`.
- Default build is offline; anything needing the network goes behind a feature (`harness`, `github`, `serve`).
- Tests never touch the network without a feature gate.
- `src/server/` is the only production surface; no GitHub Actions distribution path.
- `presets/` review policy is data, not code.
